name: janction-render
description: Cloud GPU render farm for Blender for AI agents: the remote MCP connector plus a workflow skill. .blend, bpy or glTF/FBX/USD in; frames or MP4 out.

interface.longDescription:
JANCTION Render is a cloud GPU render farm for Blender, built for AI agents. The agent writes or receives a Blender scene as a bpy Python script or a .blend file, previews it in seconds on a JANCTION GPU, estimates how long the final render will take, then renders the frames or an MP4 and returns download links that work for 24 hours.

Typical flow: scene_info reads cameras, frame range, objects, lights and missing files without rendering. render_preview returns up to 4 frames tiled in one image so the agent can check camera, lighting and materials and fix the scene before spending GPU time. render_estimate reports the expected GPU seconds, the queue wait and whether the job fits today's quota. render_final renders PNG frames or an MP4 animation. render_status reports progress and the remaining time, render_download returns the links, render_cancel stops a job, and billing / render_info report quota usage and worker availability.

Intended users: people building 3DCG with Blender who have no GPU or whose local rendering is slow, and agents that need a rendered image or video from a Blender scene. Not for non-Blender workloads such as video conversion, image generation or modeling advice.

Beta limits: 10 GPU-minutes per key per day and up to 240 frames at 1080p per job. Blender 5.0 with Cycles on NVIDIA GPUs. No account is needed: connecting creates a key. Inputs and results are deleted 24 hours after last use and are never used for training. Operated by JasmyLab Inc. (Tokyo, Japan).
capabilities: Render Blender scenes on cloud GPUs
Preview up to 4 frames in seconds
Estimate render time and quota before rendering
Render animations to MP4 or PNG frames
Inspect .blend files and bpy scripts without rendering
defaultPrompt: Make a red cube rotating on a grey floor in Blender and show me a 4-frame preview.
How long would 120 frames at 1280x720 with 64 samples take to render, and does it fit today's quota?
Render my Blender scene to a 48-frame MP4 at 1280x720.
